introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: Answer ALL the questions in the spaces provided (10 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: Answer ALL FOUR questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.
enonce_intro_markdown: Given the universal set, $\xi=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\}$ and the sets, $A=\{2,3,5,7\}$ and $B=\{2,4,6,8\}$, find:

questions.corrige_markdown:
$A\cap B$ is the set of elements that belong to both $A$ and $B$. Only $2$ is in both sets.

**Answer: $A\cap B=\{2\}$.**

$A\cup B$ is the set of elements that belong to $A$ or to $B$ (or both). List each element once.

$A\cup B=\{2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}$.

**Answer: $A\cup B=\{2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: c) $n(A\cup B)$. *[5 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$n(A\cup B)$ is the number of elements of $A\cup B=\{2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}$: there are $7$.

Check with the formula: $n(A)+n(B)-n(A\cap B)=4+4-1=7$.

**Answer: $n(A\cup B)=7$.**
